v1.feedback: The voilà concept lands — the implode/hold/bloom cycle is a genuine structural swerve, not just a palette swap, and the amber→cyan to magenta→gold flip is restrained enough. But the base form is still concentric spherical shells, which reads as a decorated noise blob for the ~80% of time outside the surprise window; give the shells distinct geometry (spiraling logarithmic shell curves, nautilus cross-sections) so 'voilà shells' has recognizable form even at rest. The mic-reactive energy scaling is nice but the tangential swirl flattens into uniform orbital mush — try making each shell's swirl axis tilt differently so the silhouette stays complex. Drop particle count per shell or tighten the radii so the form is denser and more legible rather than a diffuse haze.

v2.feedback: The nautilus logarithmic-spiral form is mathematically legible and the implode→hold→bloom surprise with the amber/cyan→magenta/gold palette flip genuinely delivers the 'voilà swerve' brief. Two issues to fix: the crossR random scatter in the shell cross-section softens the spiral ridges into puffy tubes — replace the uniform random with a tight Gaussian or trace discrete septa lines so each whorl reads as a crisp nautilus chamber. The implode phase collapses everything to r=0.3, which is exactly the noise-blob failure mode for ~1s; instead implode into a small but still-spiral form (scale the spiral radius rather than lerping to a point) so silhouette is never lost. Without mic input the piece is a slow orbit with no energy — consider a fallback procedural pulse so the review screenshot isn't dead.
